points.description: Regularized set operations keep the result a valid solid with properly defined boundaries: no dangling edges/faces (no lower-dimensional parts left hanging), e.g. after intersection of two objects.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says the result is a valid/closed solid without mentioning boundaries or dangling edges.

points.description: No edges are created extra and none are lost during the operation (e.g. intersection of two objects), so the process follows a defined, predefined sequence and gives consistent results.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says it gives correct/consistent results or follows a defined process, without the idea of no extra or lost edges.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need both ideas: boundaries well defined with no dangling edges, and no edges extra or lost in the operation, giving a defined process. Give part marks for a vague statement such as 'gives a valid solid' or 'ensures correct results'. Give 0 for unrelated or wrong answers, e.g. only naming union/intersection/difference without saying why regularization helps.
